bull_bear.body: Total borrowing ₹1,510cr (from ₹1,621cr) — split ~₹700cr structured term loan + ~₹800cr working capital. Net worth ₹1,372cr → roughly ~1.1x gearing (HIGH LEVERAGE; deleveraging in progress). WC efficiency gains (inventory −₹110cr, receivables −₹65cr) freed cash. ₹36cr promoter equity infusion via 24.7 lakh convertible warrants to LNJ Textile Advisory LLP (promoter group, ~+2.5% stake) — signalling confidence. GreenPET kept majority-debt-funded to preserve balance sheet. No dividend mention. Adani Power investment within financial assets (₹387cr).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation (debt central)

bull_bear.body:
- **Commodity/cost:** elevated gas price (post-Gulf-War), volatile cotton/poly-cotton yarn, dyes/chemicals, freight; pass-through lag hurts denim/knit spreads.
- **Demand:** soft global discretionary demand; US-tariff overhang on indirect export volumes; revenue degrowth sharper than peers.
- **Leverage:** ₹1,510cr borrowings; new ₹427cr capex adds ~₹300cr debt; deleveraging dependent on cash generation.
- **Geopolitics/energy:** Gulf-War-linked gas availability/route risk; RoDTEP withdrawn for part-year; cotton import duty.
- **Value-add erosion:** value-added products commoditise quickly.
- **FTA timing:** FTAs are expectancy, not yet realised.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident-but-cautious; emphatic this is a genuine operational (not cyclical/optical) turnaround driven by internal actions, not market tailwinds. Candid on denim/knit pain, gas costs, value-add being <20%, and WC being higher than pure-yarn peers. Promoter warrant infusion framed as confidence signal. Repeated "RSWM 2.0", "quality of earnings over volume", "double-digit EBITDA at the earliest."
bull_bear.title: Management tone

bull_bear.body:
- Reported PAT ₹52cr flattered by ₹23cr one-off deferred-tax reversal → normalised ~₹29cr (margin ~0.6%); the "turnaround to profit" is real but thinner than headline.
- ~₹250cr revenue voluntarily exited (Chhata spinning) — degrowth partly deliberate, not all demand loss.
- US exposure is indirect (sells yarn/fabric to exporting garmenters) — so both the hit and recovery are second-order.
- Value-added share honestly admitted at <20% and prone to commoditisation — quality-of-earnings story still early.
- GreenPET deliberately downsized (₹700cr→₹427cr) and pushed into RSWM (vs Bhilwara Energy) for recycled-fibre synergy; kept 70% debt to avoid large equity dilution.
- Consolidated power cost < standalone due to BG Wind Pvt Ltd captive wind entity.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious points

bull_bear.body:
- Deleveraging trend on the historical charts: Total Debt of Rs 1,103 Cr (FY22), 1,151 (FY23), 1,777 (FY24), 1,622 (FY25) and 1,510 Cr (FY26), against Net Worth rising from Rs 999 Cr (FY22) to Rs 1,372 Cr (FY26).
- Cash generation recovered sharply: Net Operational Cash Flow of Rs 210 Cr (FY22), 89 (FY23), (72) (FY24), 410 (FY25) and 428 Cr (FY26), while Net Working Capital was reduced from Rs 509 Cr (FY23) to Rs 254 Cr (FY26).
- Returns remain well below the FY22 peak - ROCE of 13.8% (FY22), 7.5%, 3.3%, 2.2% and 5.1% (FY26); ROE of 24.0% (FY22), 8.6%, 2.7%, (3.2%) and 3.8% (FY26); fixed asset turnover of 3.8x (FY22) easing to 3.1x (FY26) on Capital Employed of Rs 3,468 Cr in FY26.
- Growth capital is being part-funded by the promoter rather than fresh debt - Rs 36.06 Cr of convertible warrants to LNJ Textiles Advisory LLP at Rs 146 per warrant.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Global textile in a "soft patch" — demand normalising, not sharply recovering; Western discretionary spend cautious. Domestic relatively resilient (₹774cr Q4 stable). Export recovery early-stage (+11.4% QoQ). US-tariff cycle disrupted garment export orders (RSWM exposure indirect — sells yarn/fabric to garmenters/weavers who export); recovery "under way," ~2 more quarters to normalcy. Inventory normalisation and better visibility in select sectors noted.
business.title: Demand

business.body:
- **Synthetic/blended yarn:** domestic-skewed, less affected; optimal utilisation; spread maintained.
- **Cotton/melange yarn:** melange hit hardest (much is deemed-export to garmenters); util 65–70%; spreads broadly maintained.
- **Fabric/knit:** worst hit in FY26 (util <80%); ₹92cr expansion adding printing; FTAs + tariff settlement expected to drive recovery.
- **Denim:** most affected by gas disruption (lost production days in March) + cost inflation on 4–5 fronts (gas, dyes/chemicals, freight, yarn — cotton & poly-cotton); cost pass-through lags booked orders, compressing spreads; util >80%.
- **Power/captive:** ~70% of energy mix now renewable (wind/solar + Adani RTC tie-up); Adani Power ~₹1/unit saving on ~3–5 lakh units/day (~₹1cr/month); ₹60cr renewable investment cited.
- **Sustainable textile / recycled fibre:** produces 130 t/day polyester fibre from ~60 lakh recycled PET bottles/day; domestic-skewed; underpins GreenPET project synergy.
business.title: Segment commentary (yarn / fabric / denim / power)

business.body:
- Gas/energy volatility → renewable (wind/solar) + Adani RTC power tie-up; BG Wind captive — beneficiaries: ⭐ RSWM's own renewable mix, Adani Power.
- US-tariff / China+1 + UK/EU/NZ FTAs → Indian textile exporters broadly (RSWM indirect via garmenters). ✅
- PET-bottle waste / sustainability mandates → recycled-PET fibre / GreenPET (RSWM). ⭐
- Income Tax Act 2025 concessional regime → structural PAT tailwind FY27+. ✅

---
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries

business.body:
- Three business verticals under one integrated model - Yarn (since 1960), Denim (since 2007) and Knitted Fabric (since 2023) - branded on the cover as "YARN | DENIM | KNITS".
- CMD Riju Jhunjhunwala frames the moat as "Our integrated business model, customer-centric approach, and continued focus on value-added and sustainable products", reinforcing "RSWM's position as a leading integrated textile manufacturer".
- CFO cites sector tailwinds: "stable cotton prices, improving export enquiries and gradual normalization of international demand" and "India's growing position as a preferred global sourcing destination, supported by its strong manufacturing ecosystem and favourable policy initiatives".
- Segment revenue mix (including inter-segment) for Q1 FY27 is Yarn 77.8% / Fabric 22.2%, versus Yarn 77.3% / Fabric 22.7% in Q1 FY26 and Yarn 78.8% / Fabric 21.2% in Q4 FY26.
- Synthetic Yarn is described as "Key Contributor of RSWM's revenue" and "a key pillar of the company's long-term vision", with over 60 years in the division.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Transformation programme] "RSWM 2.0 was launched with a new management team under the vision: REFLECT, RESTORE, RESHAPE" (2025); the CFO describes Q1 performance as reflecting "the steady execution of the RSWM 2.0 transformation strategy" and the JMD calls it an "encouraging turnaround".
- [Acquisition] 2026 acquisition of 100% equity in LNJ GreenPET Pvt. Ltd. adds a non-textile, recycled-PET business line as a subsidiary - a new segment relative to the yarn/denim/knits base.
- [M&A track record] Long-running acquisition strategy: Rishabhdev plant from HEG Limited (2003), Jaipur Polyspin and Mordi Textiles & Processors (2005), BG Wind Power (2024), Ginni Filaments' Chhata undertaking (2024), Birla Advanced Knits machinery (FY26) and LNJ GreenPET (2026).
- [Leadership] Named executives are Mr. Riju Jhunjhunwala (CMD), Mr. Rajeev Gupta (JMD) and Mr. Nitin Tulyani (President & CFO).
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: GP margin 38.1% (+246 bps FY26) on RM-cost discipline (−9.5%) and better H2 spreads. EBITDA margin 7.1% FY26 (+231 bps). Power/fuel −₹17.6cr FY26 via renewables. Key cost pressures: gas cost stepped up sharply post-Gulf-War (availability restored by April, but price elevated), dyes/chemicals, freight, yarn prices — all squeezing denim spreads via pass-through lag. Income Tax Act 2025 → concessional 25.17% rate from FY27 (structural tax tailwind ahead).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Rev ₹1,142cr (+4.5% QoQ, −9.1% YoY); EBITDA ₹85cr, margin 7.4% (+115bps YoY). FY26: Rev ₹4,554cr (−5.6%), EBITDA ₹327cr (+40.5%, margin 7.1%), PAT ₹52cr rptd / ~₹29cr norm (vs −₹41cr loss FY25) — TURNAROUND YEAR. Borrowings down to ₹1,510cr (−₹111cr). One-offs: ₹23cr DTL reversal, ₹250cr Chhata revenue exit, ₹51cr other income (asset sale). Utilisation: melange 65–70%, denim >80%, knit <80%. Capex: ₹92cr knit/printing (Q3FY27), ₹427cr GreenPET Ratlam (op. Q1 next FY, 70:30). Promoter ₹36cr warrant infusion. Guidance: double-digit-EBITDA aspiration; deleverage term loan over 3–4 yrs; Q1FY27 ≈ flat-to-slightly-better.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **Volume/utilisation:** denim, knit, melange each expected to improve ~7–10% utilisation off Q4 base; current quarter (Q1FY27) "slightly better or equivalent to last quarter."
- **Margin:** double-digit EBITDA is the stated aspiration "as early as possible" (no dated target); requires demand recovery + internal efficiency + product development + supply-chain sourcing combined.
- **Value-added mix:** currently <1/5 (≈20%) of sales; value-added products commoditise fast — continuous development needed; no quantified mix target.
- **Deleveraging:** ~₹700cr structured term loan (denim/knit/Banswara Kapas expansion) to be "minimised" over next 3–4 years; WC ~₹800cr being worked down.
- **Capex:** no major fresh capex beyond (i) ₹92cr knit/printing expansion (capacity 600→900 t; ~120t printing; commissioning Q3FY27; +3–4% EBITDA in knit) and (ii) ₹427cr GreenPET / recycled-PET B2B plant at Ratlam, MP (construction starts mid-May, operational Q1 next FY; funded 70:30 — ₹300cr loan approved, ₹127cr equity+holdco loan); plus routine modernisation/replacement capex (1–3 yr payback discipline).
- **Topline aspiration:** ₹6,200–6,500cr in 3–4 years deemed "possible" (analyst-led, mgmt agreed).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- **Value-added yarn/products:** mix <20%; commoditisation risk; continuous development thrust ("RSWM 2.0").
- **Exports / FTAs:** UK, EU, New Zealand (and Australia) FTAs are upside optionality — "yet to be reality," implementation expected late this year / early next; new markets added (Europe, Sri Lanka, 2 US denim customers).
- **GreenPET / recycled-PET B2B (Ratlam):** scaled down from ~₹700cr to ₹427cr; in-house synergy with existing recycled-fibre operations.
- **Deleveraging:** finance cost −9.2%; term-loan run-off over 3–4 yrs.
- **Knit + printing:** new product segment, +3–4% knit EBITDA from H2FY27.
outlook.title: Growth / optionality

deepdive.thesis: FY26 turnaround year — moved from a loss to positive PAT by trading volume for profitable mix, deleveraging, and shifting ~70% of energy to renewables; FY27 thesis hinges on denim/knit/melange utilisation recovery, double-digit-EBITDA aspiration, and the ₹427cr GreenPET (recycled-PET B2B) capex de-risking via a 70:30 debt-equity structure.

open.item: Approved installation of a behind-the-meter 9.6 MW solar power facility at a capital outlay of ₹25 crore.
Ongoing modernisation capex of ₹53.28 crore across various units; ₹47.03 crore incurred in FY26 with the balance to be spent in FY27.
The synthetic yarn division will begin producing Graphene yarn in FY27, a strategic move expected to boost profitability and strengthen competitive edge.
Melange Yarn division is undertaking capacity enhancements in yarn dyeing and compact yarns to capture emerging demand for specialised yarns.
Plans to strengthen energy efficiency initiatives in FY27 through expansion of automation systems and targeted operational improvements across strategically identified sites.
₹427 crore GreenPET project at Ratlam, Madhya Pradesh, to deepen recycled-fibre / sustainability credentials with global brand customers.
Company states an ambition of building towards ₹5,000 crore in revenue, supported by EU/US/UK trade-agreement tailwinds.

Board approved raising ₹36.06 crore via issuance of up to 24,70,000 fresh convertible warrants to Promoter/Promoter Group on preferential basis, subject to shareholder approval at an EGM scheduled 8 May 2026.

Company entered a new agreement to sell its Thermal Power Plant assets to Malik Heights, replacing an earlier arrangement with Didwania Trading Company that could not lift the assets, as part of monetising stranded assets.
LNJ Greenpet (wholly owned subsidiary) is implementing a recycling project at a project cost of ₹427 crore at Ratlam, Madhya Pradesh, as forward integration to the recycled polyester fibre business.

Board approved (6 May 2026) formulation of the RSWM Limited Employee Stock Option Plan 2026 for grant of up to 9,70,000 options to eligible employees of the Company and its subsidiaries, subject to shareholder and regulatory approval.

risks.note: FY26 operating environment was marked by U.S. tariff disruptions and RoDTEP adjustments impacting the garmenting supply chain and export demand; management cites these as external headwinds that softened export demand in the first half of the year.
risks.risk: Trade-policy and tariff exposure on exports

risks.note: Domestic cotton prices remained range-bound but subject to intermittent volatility driven by global price trends, import parity and Cotton Corporation of India procurement operations, directly affecting spinning input costs.

Melange yarn utilisation stood at only 65-70% (targeted to reach 85-90% by early FY27), Knitting operated below 80% utilisation, and value-added products account for less than 20% of sales — representing structural headroom but also current margin drag if utilisation/mix does not improve as planned.
risks.risk: Underutilised capacity / low value-added product mix

risks.note: The closure of spinning operations at the Chhata unit removed a structurally low-margin volume source but resulted in an approximate ₹250 crore reduction in revenue, illustrating the trade-off risk embedded in the Company's ongoing portfolio rationalisation.
risks.risk: Revenue volatility from strategic asset rationalisation

risks.note: The Company is still transitioning away from legacy coal-based boilers to biofuel-powered systems and expanding renewable power sourcing; until this transition is complete, power and fuel costs remain a variable structural exposure, even though recent initiatives have begun reducing this cost base.
risks.risk: Energy and fuel cost exposure during transition
